title: Operator delegation lifecycle and proof catalog — PRD (WIP)
content:
Summary:

This doc sketches a PRD for an operator delegation lifecycle and an associated proof catalog used when customers run Redwood Private in a customer-managed network (VPC/on‑prem). Goal: provide a lightweight, auditable flow that lets operators (customer admins / delegated Redwood operators) perform necessary network and configuration tasks while generating verifiable minimal evidence for audit, approval gates, and forensic replay.

Problems we see today:
- Onboarding often stalls because security teams request too much raw telemetry or entire VM snapshots. The team needs smaller, structured evidence artifacts.
- Delegated operator actions (e.g., install agents, rotate keys, change egress IPs) lack consistent proof semantics — different teams ship different logs or callouts.
- Approval gates are binary; they don't capture partial approvals, time-boxed delegations, or compensating controls.
- Audits want a simple way to assert: who did what, with what consent, and what changed in the customer-managed network.

Principles and constraints:
- Minimality: evidence should be as small as possible while preserving investigability. Prefer signed assertions and short hashes over full packet captures.
- Privacy: do not collect PII or customer payloads. Evidence must be metadata + config diffs + limited snapshots when strictly necessary.
content_addendum:
(continued)

High-level product goals (success metrics):
- Reduce time-to-approval for operator-driven onboarding steps from median 6 days -> 24 hours for 70% of cases.
- Provide a set of canonical proof artifacts that satisfy basic audit requests for 90% of SOC 2-style reviews without additional data pulls.
- Support time-boxed delegation tokens and explicit scope enforcement in the approval gate UI.

Scope (what this PRD covers):
- Delegation lifecycle: request, grant (time/scoped), perform, attest, revoke, and evidence archival.
- Proof catalog: canonical evidence artifact types, retention suggestions, schema examples, and UX snippets for evidence review.
- Approval gate model: multi-step, multi-signatory, conditional approvals (e.g., allow agent install if fallback region configured).

Out of scope:
- Deep forensic tools (packet-level replay) — only surface-level snapshot artifacts.
- Full legal/compliance sign-off. We will collaborate with Legal for templates but won't onboard legal workflows here.

Actors and roles:
- Customer Admin: requests and reviews delegations; can sign approvals.
- Operator (delegated): performs actions in customer-managed environment using a delegation token; produces proof artifacts.
- Auditor: internal customer or 3rd-party who will inspect proof catalog entries.
- Redwood Control Plane: issues tokens, stores signed assertions, ingests indexed metadata for search.

User stories (examples):
- As a Customer Admin, I want to issue a time-bound delegation to Redwood Support for a package install that only permits package installation and keeps port changes disallowed. I want an evidentiary bundle at completion keyed to that delegation.
- As a delegated Operator, I want a CLI flow that mints a signed evidence bundle upon completion of the task and uploads it to the customer's allowed evidence sink (S3/HTTPS endpoint).
- As an Auditor, I want to query the control plane for a specific delegation token and retrieve all proof artifacts and a human-readable summary.

Lifecycle model (flow):
1) Request: Customer Admin raises a delegation request via Console or API. Request includes target resource (operator cluster id), allowed action set, duration, and optional preconditions (e.g. must have 2FA).
2) Approval: Console supports single/dual sign-off, optional conditional rules, and delegation templates. Approval produces a delegation token (JWT-like) with scope claims.
3) Execute: Operator uses token to perform actions. Each action call generates a signed local assertion (signed with operator key) describing the action and the minimal artifact (config diff, service PID, checksums).
4) Attest: On completion, operator submits an evidence bundle to configured evidence sink; control plane ingests a compact index record (not full artifact).
5) Review & Retention: Customer Admin or Auditor reviews artifacts in Console. Policy-driven retention moves artifacts to longer-term cold store or prunes per retention SLA.
6) Revoke/Audit: Token revocation path exists; revocations are published to an immutable ledger (hash chain) and surfaced in the audit timeline.

Proof catalog (canonical artifact types):
- Delegation Assertion (DA): Signed token showing requestor, approver(s), scope, duration, issuance timestamp, and approval metadata. (store as JSON-LD-like string; keep compact).
- Action Record (AR): Single-line signed record for an atomic change. Fields: action_id, actor_id, timestamp, action_type, target_resource, pre_state_checksum, post_state_checksum, short_notes (free text up to 300 chars).
- Config Diff Patch (CDP): Unified diff-like patch of changed configuration files (text only). Include pre/post checksums and an optional small base64 encoded snippet if truncated.
- Evidence Snapshot (ES): Minimal frozen snapshot when required (service process list, listening ports, config fragments). Max size target: 200KB compressed.
- Proof Index (PI): Control-plane indexed metadata: delegation_id, action_count, artifact_types, artifact_checksums, retention_policy_ref. This is what we ingest and index — not raw snapshot content.

Evidence schema examples (human-readable):
- DA example: delegation_id=dlg-20241015-07; issued_by=customer-admin:alice@example.com; approvers=[sec-lead:bob@example.com]; scope=[install:package=redwood-agent, ports=none]; expires=2024-10-16T20:00Z; signature=(sig).
- AR example: action_id=ar-00014; actor=operator-liam; ts=2024-10-15T12:22:31Z; action_type=install-package; target=cluster-42/node-3; pre_checksum=sha256:...; post_checksum=sha256:...; notes="installed v0.9.2, verified service health"; sig=(sig).

Approval gate variants and rules:
- Template gates: pre-packaged flows for common ops (agent install, key rotation, egress change). Templates define required approvers, evidence types, and whether live escrow snapshot required.
- Conditional gates: allow auto-approval if automated checks pass (e.g., preflight CI verifies package checksum + security-scan).
- Multi-signer gates: require N-of-M approvers with time-window constraints.
- Rollback-aware gates: approvals can include a required rollback plan and an execution window, otherwise gate rejects.

Operational telemetry & indexing:
- Control plane will only index Proof Index entries. Artifacts are pushed to customer-controlled sinks by operator; optional ephemeral upload to Redwood for diagnostics (customer opts in).
- Audit timeline logs (non-sensitive): delegation events (requested, approved, executed, evidence_uploaded, revoked).
- Sampling: long-running maintenance operations should produce sampled detailed logs; sample rate is policy-controlled and surfaced in the evidence bundle.

Retention and compliance guidance (recommended defaults):
- Delegation Assertion (DA): retain 3 years for enterprise customers (default), configurable down to 90 days for small customers.
- Action Record (AR): 180 days default; extendable for regulatory customers.
- Config Diff Patch (CDP)/Evidence Snapshot (ES): 90 days default; if a compliance flag is set, snapshot retention escalates.
- Proof Index (PI): kept for searchability 3+ years at minimal storage cost. PI has no sensitive content by design.

UX and Console interactions (sketches in prose):
- Request form: quick select templates, optional free-text justification, preflight checklist (auto-run security/compatibility checks).
- Approval screen: shows compact summary of required artifacts and the expected evidence size; allows reviewer to require additional evidence or restrict scope before signing.
- Evidence viewer: shows proof index entries with badges for "minimal", "snapshot included", or "requires deeper review". Clicking a badge opens a timeline and hash-verified download link (customer-managed location).

Developer/implementation notes (engineers):
- Delegation tokens: JWT with custom 'delegation' claim; signed by control-plane key and bound to resource id & allowed actions. Tokens should have short TTL and support revocation lists.
- Local operator agent: small CLI shim that signs action records with an ephemeral operator key (rotated per session) and bundles artifacts. Provide SDK for customers who want to run the operator from their own tooling.
- Immutable ledger: lightweight append-only log with hash chaining for revocation events and delegation issuance; ledger stored encrypted in customer tenant and mirrored in the Redwood control plane for search.
- Evidence sink connectors: S3 (presigned), HTTPS endpoint (mutual TLS), and customer SIEM forwarder.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: delegation request + approval UI with templates for 3 common ops (agent install, key rotation, egress change).
- Control plane: issue delegation token, store proof index records, show audit timeline.
- Operator flow: CLI shim that creates Action Records and uploads Evidence Snapshot to a configured S3 presigned URL.
- Auditor UX: retrieve delegation_id -> list of PI entries -> download evidence link (customer endpoint).

Risks & open questions:
- Q: How much control do customers require over the content of Action Records? A: expose a redactable fields policy and a schema versioning mechanism.
- Q: Does retention policy cause legal complexity for certain jurisdictions? Need Legal check for EU data laws.
- Risk: Customers may incorrectly assume Redwood stores raw artifacts. We must clearly document default behavior: Redwood only indexes PI and does not retain raw artifacts unless explicitly configured.

Next steps / proposed milestones:
- Design spike (2 weeks): implement token schema, minimal AR schema and CLI shim prototype.
- Security review (1 week): legal & security signoff on minimal artifact content.
- Pilot with 2 customers (4–6 weeks): instrument templates and retention profiles; collect feedback.
- Iterate to Beta (2 months): add multi-signer gates, conditional rules, and evidence viewer refinements.

Appendix: quick checklist for pilot:
- Pick 2 customers:1 on AWS VPC, 1 on customer-managed colo.
- Implement S3 presigned evidence sink + test uploads.
- Run simulated approval flows with 3 operator actions per customer.
- Measure time-to-approval and artifact sizes; target median bundle < 200KB per action.

Open links & refs:
- related: CONFLUENCE-12345 (delegation concepts), JIRA-PD-987 (pilot ticket), GH PR #214 (cli-shim prototype).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep artifacts tiny; auditors prefer structured assertions to big zips.
- Think about future: zero-knowledge proof to attest actions without revealing sensitive pre/post state? Long term.
- Need a small UX research session: 3 security reviewers to validate acceptance criteria before pilot.

----
End of draft (WIP).
